issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a terrorism trauma, sexual-violence comments as a primary trigger is hard to reconcile unless the index event also involved sexual assault or closely related content; nothing else in the profile supports that connection.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: The appraisal of betrayal by a trusted person is difficult to fit with terrorism as the trauma type unless there was a clear interpersonal betrayal component; the rest of the selected items describe loss of control, helplessness, avoidance, dissociation, and substance use rather than interpersonal betrayal.

vignette: Rahul, a 37-year-old South Asian male and a psychologist, experienced a traumatic event that has profoundly affected his life. He was working late one evening when an act of terrorism unfolded in his city, with gunshots echoing through the streets near his office building. The chaos and panic during this event led to a sense of intense helplessness, as he felt completely out of control amidst the cacophony of gunfire. This experience has left Rahul haunted by specific triggers that activate his distress. Since the incident, nighttime has become a particularly frightening time for Rahul. He wakes up frequently in the dark, feeling a sense of vulnerability and fear, replaying the sounds of gunshots in his mind. These triggers have led him to adopt maladaptive strategies as coping mechanisms. When faced with these overwhelming feelings, he often turns to drinking alcohol or taking medication, seeking a way to numb the emotional pain and escape into a world of his own making. His distress is further compounded by negative appraisals that have taken root in his psyche. Rahul has come to believe that he cannot stop bad things from happening to him, which leaves him feeling both helpless and unrecognizable as the person he once was. This sense of helplessness exacerbates his maladaptive behaviors; when he feels out of control, he finds solace in substances and fantasy, further reinforcing these coping mechanisms. The world around Rahul has also become more dangerous in his perception, making every sound or night a potential trigger for intense anxiety and fear. The auditory triggers of gunfire have extended to everyday noises that remind him of the traumatic event, causing him significant distress at work and home. His wife notices changes in his behavior—how he becomes withdrawn and drinks heavily after waking up in the middle of the night. The reinforcing cycle is clear: when Rahul feels triggered by lack of control or auditory cues, he turns to substances to escape, which only reinforces his negative beliefs about himself and the world. He has become increasingly isolated at work, often avoiding interactions that might trigger stressful memories, leading to a deterioration in his professional relationships. His colleagues have noticed this change, commenting on how distant and distracted Rahul seems. Rahul’s maladaptive strategies further exacerbate his triggers. After drinking heavily, he finds himself more sensitive to the slightest noise, making it even harder for him to sleep or feel safe during nighttime hours. This vicious cycle has led to significant changes in his daily life—his work performance has declined, and his marriage is strained. Despite these challenges, what finally brought Rahul to seek help was a sense of desperation and fear that he would continue down this destructive path indefinitely. He hopes for a way out of the overwhelming distress and a return to feeling like himself again. The prospect of therapy offers him a glimmer of hope amidst the darkness—a chance to regain control over his life and find peace in the world once more.
